text: CONTRADICTION SETTLED: the stance-mastery domain is [0,10], not [1,10]. The 1 in StatsManager.as:740-742 (IntStat(1000,1)/(1001,1)/(1002,1)) is a NEW-PLAYER DEFAULT, not an index base - the enclosing function is initNewPlayer at StatsManager.as:689. For NPCs the value comes from XMLNpc.getMastery, which ends 'return 0;' at :685 when the npc carries no matching <skill> row, and a census of reference/extracted/npcdata.xml shows only 76 of 495 <npc> rows carry skill 1000 (77 carry 1001, 79 carry 1002; of those that do, 74 each are at <lvl>10</lvl> and the rest at 2-3). So 419 of 495 npcs evaluate the stance curve at mastery 0. EnemyElite.as:89 declares 'var balancedMastery:int = 0;' before its getMastery reads at :103-105, and the web fighter class declares all three fields '= 0' at §1t99s0§.as:107/:109/:111. This is NOT a build-parity split: web v0.717 and android v0.682 agree the field is a plain int defaulting to 0. Consequence for the rewrite: a config that clamps mastery to >= 1 mis-prices every generic mob's stance damage AND reach - Light damage would floor at 0.54 instead of 0.50 and Heavy reach at 0.54x instead of 0.50x of base. The mastery-10 CEILING is unaffected and stands.

text: RR:161-163 item 3 tells the next build session to 'either model the mastery curve or decide-and-flag "the build targets mastery-9"'. The curve is in the payload, it is linear, and it reproduces BOTH ends of the ledger's own table. §1t99s0§.as:3258-3271: base = minDamage + Math.random() * damageRange; Light = base * (0.5 + 0.4 * lightMastery * 0.1); Balanced = base * (1 + 0.2 * balancedMastery * 0.1); Heavy, Dual and Reversed all = base * 1.4 flat. At mastery 0 that is exactly the ledger's level-1 Shugyosha row 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.4; at mastery 10 it is exactly the ledger's ceiling row 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4. The identical shape governs reach (0.5 + 0.04m for Heavy, 1 + 0.02m for Balanced, flat 1.4 for Light), so one linear rule covers both tables. This CONFIRMS the ledger's item 3 rather than overturning it, but it removes the fork: model the curve, do not flag a mastery-9 target. Build divergence to respect: android MCSPlayer.as:3205-3213 uses 0.5 + 0.5*m*0.01 and 1 + 0.5*m*0.01 on a 0-100 mastery scale with Heavy at 1.5, so the android coefficients must not be ported.

text: A MEASURED INSTANCE OF THE S0-3 PARITY HOLE, and the strongest one this lane has. The per-stat add-button ceilings are NOT the same in the two builds. Web v0.717 §1t5957s0§.as:3341-3346: HP < 10 + (lvl+10)*10, CHI < 10 + (lvl+10)*5, AP < 30 + (lvl+10)*5, ATK/DEF/SPD < 1 + (lvl+10)*3. At level 80 that is web 271 versus android 90 for ATK/DEF/SPD — a 3x divergence — plus 910 vs 460 HP and 480 vs 90 AP. The two blocks are otherwise line-for-line twins (same six buttons, same order, same 'more than two capped' nag), so this is deliberate retuning between v0.682 and v0.717, not a decompiler artifact. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LANE: the S0-3 caveat's warning that 'combat tuning parity is NOT established' now has a concrete counterexample. Any progression or combat number ported from an android-only artifact must be treated as v0.682 until a web line says otherwise. Only CHI's formula survives the version change unchanged.

text: art-anim-audio-feel/rig-is-19-nodes (UPHELD) says the rig 'keys 19 nodes per pose in the stance sets (20 in the human set)'. The human set does not key 20 per pose. Census over all 158 <anim> rows in the human blob reference/extracted/bindata/108_1t4635s0.bin, counting <n> records per <f> frame: the per-anim maximum is 20 in only 2 anims, 19 in 130, 18 in 10, 17 in 13 and 13 in 3. Worse for a fixed-rig renderer, 44 of the 158 anims have a per-frame node count that VARIES within the clip, and some frames carry ZERO <n> records at all (heavyhorizontalslash_partc, balancedhorizontalslash_partc, balancedjumpslash_parta, sheathesword, backstep, forwardstep, katanajump all bottom out at 0). The two severance deaths are the sharpest case: deathnohead is 23 frames of 17 nodes then 8 frames of exactly ONE node (i=16), deathnohand is 23 frames of 17 then 2 frames of 3, while deathinhalf holds 17 across all 28. So a node record is a PER-FRAME DELTA LIST, not a full skeleton pose, and a renderer that resets unlisted joints each frame will tear the corpse apart on the tail of every dismemberment clip.
